three_additions_the_amendment_did_not_re: Voluntariness is expressly conditional: ASIC states it 'may consider using compulsory powers to achieve a complete register, if required'. The amendment treats voluntary supply as a fixed property of the mechanism; on ASIC's own account it is a current setting, not a settled one.

The published field is tri-state, not binary. ASIC states the PRS shows (a) a principal website and other websites if provided, (b) whether a licensee does not operate a website, and (c) whether a licensee has not yet supplied addresses. Coverage therefore has three cells, and 'no website shown' is not by itself evidence of non-participation.

ASIC's own FAQ promises a bulk route: 'Data will be available to download as a list via the Australian government's data.gov.au.' As at 2026-08-02 the website field is not in that dataset (see machine_readability).

fields_observed: Websites section with 'Principal website' and 'Other websites' (present only where more than the principal website is held)
professional_registers_search.rendering: client-rendered single-page application; the HTTP response body is a 2,217-byte shell containing no register data (raw/prs_374409.html)
professional_registers_search.internal_json_endpoint: POST /search/screenservices/Search/Detail/EntityDetail/DataActionGetEntityDetail returns a structured Website object {HasWebsite, PrincipalWebsiteUrl, WebsiteUrlSummary}; it returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients (raw/prs_screenservice_endpoint_response.html) and was not circumvented
professional_registers_search.website_field_searchability_test: Searching the exact string the register publishes as AFSL 385620's principal website — 'fusionmarkets.com.au' — returns 'No results found.' The search accepts name, licence number, registration number, ACN or ABN. Reverse lookup from a domain to a licensee is therefore not supported.

data_gov_au.relevant_dataset: asic-afs-licensee (ASIC - Australian Financial Services Licensee Dataset), updated weekly

machine_readability.conclusion: No bulk or downloadable form of the website field exists as at 2026-08-02. What is machine-readable: the AFS licensee register minus the website field (weekly CSV/TSV/XLSX on data.gov.au, 6,525 rows). What is not machine-readable: the website field itself, which is available only through per-licensee lookup on a client-rendered, reCAPTCHA-protected search application whose underlying JSON endpoint refuses non-browser clients.

population_coverage_rate.status: NOT OBTAINABLE within this audit's discipline
population_coverage_rate.why: The headline number the mechanism's stated purpose calls for — what share of AFS licensees have supplied a website — cannot be computed because the field is not published in any bulk form. Computing it from the register as published would require roughly 6,525 individual lookups against a reCAPTCHA-protected application, which this audit will not perform.
what_would_be_needed: ASIC to add the website columns to the weekly data.gov.au AFS Licensee dataset — three fields would suffice: principal website, other websites, and the supply-status flag distinguishing 'provided', 'does not operate a website' and 'not yet supplied'. ASIC's own FAQ already states this data 'will be available to download as a list via data.gov.au'.
or a documented public read API for the PRS website field.
Either route makes the coverage rate a one-line computation against a 6,525-row frame, and makes it recomputable weekly.

unit_level_results.identification: All claim units in artifacts/verification_v1 and artifacts/verification_v2 whose displayed authority is ASIC. The full set is xs-ASIC-374409, iux-ASIC-529610, fusionmarkets-ASIC-nonumber, fpmarkets-ASIC-nonumber — confirmed by enumerating all 21 verified units.

MATCH.meaning: observation domain appears in the register's website field for the licensee whose licence the page displays

MISMATCH.meaning: the register publishes at least one website for the licensee and the observation domain is not among them

ABSENCE.meaning: the register publishes no website for the licensee, so it makes no statement either way about the observation domain

NOT-APPLICABLE.meaning: the page displays no AFS licence number and no entity for the ASIC element, so no licensee record exists to compare against

unit_level_results.note_on_the_class_A_unit: fusionmarkets-ASIC-nonumber is the one ASIC unit where the licence holder is also the operative entity for the domain (class A in verification_v2). Its observation domain still does not appear in the register's website field, because the register publishes the licensee's .com.au domain and the Chinese-language observation domain is the .com. The same .com/.com.au split appears at iux. This is a property of what the field records — a licensee's own Australian-facing addresses — not a finding about either firm.
unit_level_results.tri_state_limitation: For both records showing no website, the PRS displays the string 'No website supplied'. Which of ASIC's two published non-supply states applies — 'does not operate a website' or 'has not yet supplied' — is UNVERIFIABLE-TODAY from the rendered field. In the one record where the underlying payload was observable (374409) the HasWebsite flag was empty, which is consistent with 'not yet supplied' but is not asserted as a finding.

structural_gaps_observed.observation: Supply is voluntary and ASIC publishes no coverage figure. Two of the four ASIC licensee records this study looked up publish no website. With no bulk field, no one outside ASIC can state the coverage rate, and ASIC has not published one. ASIC states it may consider compulsory powers if required.

ASIC states that AR websites are not included. This study's own frame shows why that boundary is load-bearing: two of the four ASIC licensee records carry authorised-representative entries, and verification_v2 recorded a second, ceased record for one licensee on the authorised-representatives register. A domain operated under an AR appointment cannot be checked against this field at all.

structural_gaps_observed.gap: the field is not searchable by domain
structural_gaps_observed.observation: Not previously recorded anywhere in this study. The PRS accepts name, licence number, registration number, ACN or ABN; searching a published website string returns no results. The verification the stated purpose describes — someone holding a domain from an advertisement and asking which licensee it belongs to — is a reverse lookup the register does not support. Every check must start from a licensee identity the enquirer already has.

language_discipline: Every statement above is of the form 'this domain does / does not appear in this register field', with the register URL and the check date. No brand is described as fraudulent, fake, misleading or a scam. No inference of unlicensed operation is drawn and Corporations Act s911A is not cited (amendment 5 §2). Absence from a register field is recorded as a register-content observation, never as a finding about a firm.
